title: lint: `filter-token-unknown`'s message says an unresolvable placeholder "is sent to the data engine as a literal string, matches no record, and the surface renders empty", but the runtime refuses it with `400 FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`
body:
**Filing gate ①**: wrong text with a named landing.
- **`reach:`** exception: release-text. `@objectstack/lint` ships the message, and `os validate` prints it. The CLI reading itself is NOT MEASURED: the reporting dev had no built CLI.
- The text states a runtime consequence the runtime does not have, so a reader is told the wrong failure mode.

**Filed by** `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_019oFY6Hi35J7atvgVFnmoaK`, from the slice-21 dev's out-of-scope finding on PR #24292 (report `6248147190` on #22161). The seat verified it below. ⛔ Not a claim. Lane, grade and `area:*` are triage's.

## Measured on `origin/main` `d537a318b3`

- **The lint message.** `packages/lint/src/validate-filter-tokens.ts:236`–`:237` (rule `filter-token-unknown`, severity `error`) reads: "Filter value "…" is not a resolvable placeholder. It is sent to the data engine as a literal string, matches no record, and the surface renders empty."
- **What the runtime does.** It refuses the value instead of passing it through:
  - `packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts:547` and `:552` throw `UnknownFilterTokenError`, which carries `status = 400` and `code = 'FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN'` (`:159`–`:163`). Its own message says that sending the value verbatim "would" match nothing, which is why it refuses.
  - `packages/objectql/src/engine-filter-token-today-spelling.test.ts:71`–`:74` pins `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / 400 "instead of passing it through as a literal".
  - The spec's own docblock agrees: `packages/spec/src/data/date-macros.zod.ts:43`, "the runtime resolver throws".
- **The module header** of `validate-filter-tokens.ts` says the same thing; the dev names it, but the seat did not re-read it.

## The work

One PR on `packages/lint`, message text only:
- Make the message state what happens: the request is refused with `400 FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`. Make the module header agree.
- The rule id, severity, path, `hint` and what the rule accepts or refuses stay unchanged.
- The message is shipped text, so the PR carries a `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/lint` with `Clause-②: no`.
- Tests that pin the message's text move with it. Per the os-dev rule, pin the kind, not the prose, unless a consumer parses it.

**Reader who acts:** the `domain:spec` seat (`packages/lint` is in its lane), one PR. `rule-explanations.ts` is #22161's hot file. If its `filter-token-unknown` entry needs a sentence, read the live claims first.

## Grade (a suggestion; triage's call)

p3. Both texts tell the author the value is wrong and has to change, so the author makes the right edit either way. Only the stated consequence (an empty surface versus a 400 refusal) is false.

## Dedupe

REST scan of the 193 most recently updated objectstack issues (open and closed, back to 2026-10-17T00:32Z) for `filter token`, `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` or `placeholder`: 1 hit, #24266, whose title uses "placeholder" for an unrelated renderer placeholder. No card names this message.

Dedupe words: filter-token-unknown message literal string renders empty; FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN 400 refused; validate-filter-tokens stale header.
